acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The refusal shape for an unbound action (RBAC visible-but-refused) is specified precisely enough for a B1-3 test to assert the exact HTTP status, body shape and audit record.
AC-2: The single-active-session state machine names both the refuse and takeover paths, states which is default, and specifies the audit record for a takeover.

AC-3: Role tokens -> bindings -> AD group references never place a corporate group name in application code; the persistence and encryption of group references names the key source by reference to C1 section 6, not redefined.

AC-4: The DIRECTORY-POSTURE service account's credential scope, storage, rotation and outage behaviour are fully specified, with the document stating explicitly that the function stays disabled pending corporate verification per D-6.
AC-5: The E1-E7 gate chain is enumerated in order with each gate's exact check, and its composition boundary with C2's pre-execution checks is stated without duplication.
AC-6: C2's owner/approver/execution-identity fields are shown resolving from this contract's session/role model with a concrete example.
AC-7: §8 gives at least ten testable acceptance criteria covering B1-3 and the B1-10 acceptance scenario (three concurrent admins, one takeover, one refuse).
AC-8: §9 lists every contradiction with frozen authority found (or states none and which documents were checked); no PO-reserved decision (DIRECTORY-POSTURE, RAW-RETENTION) is reopened.
AC-9: No identity/session/role table is redefined that C1 section 3 already owns; only C3-owned columns/semantics are specified, by reference to C1's table names.
AC-10: The document does not enable DIRECTORY-POSTURE's persisted-group-reference function; it specifies it as ready-but-disabled.

context_not_loaded: Any Java source, Gradle build, Flyway migration or Docker artefact -- B1 implements this contract
Any function this contract gates being enabled before C3 exists: DIRECTORY-POSTURE stays disabled until corporate verification is recorded, regardless of what this document specifies
Device contact, credentials, network access of any kind
The capability/step definitions themselves (C4) and the backup approval rules (C7, though C2 section 7 already names the pieces C3 must supply identities for)
invariants: RBAC is never menu-hiding: a role without a binding sees the action and a stated reason it is refused (design section 5) -- this contract specifies the refusal shape (HTTP status, body, audit record) precisely enough to test

Single active session per identity: a second login either refuses with the first session's context shown, or offers an explicit takeover that terminates the first session and is itself audited -- specify both paths and which one is default (design section 7.4's table becomes this contract's test matrix)

Role tokens -> bindings -> AD group references keep three levels of indirection: no corporate group name appears in application code, only in a binding record; specify exactly what is persisted (encrypted group refs) and where the encryption key lives (reference C1 section 6 secrets, do not redefine)

DIRECTORY-POSTURE (D-6): the read-only directory service account's credential scope, storage, rotation and outage (fail-closed vs fail-open) behaviour must be fully specified even though the function stays disabled -- 'conditional' means the spec is ready, not that the spec is skipped

E1-E7 gate chain on the HTTP layer: name what each gate checks (authentication, session validity, role binding, capability existence, action-class admissibility, target/profile approval state, connectivity/precondition) and in what order; this must compose with C2's pre-execution checks (C2 section 6) without duplicating them -- state the boundary explicitly
No decision frozen in UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md is reopened; contradictions with frozen authority are REPORTED in a dedicated section, never silently resolved

Owner/approver/execution-identity (C2 section 7.2) resolve from this contract's session/role model -- state exactly how a job's 'approver' identity is captured from an authenticated session at approval time

AC-2 single-active-session state machine names both refuse and takeover paths, states refuse-by-inaction is default, and specifies the takeover audit record via the sessions trigger (section 3.3/3.4/3.5); AC-3 role tokens -> bindings -> AD group references never place a corporate group name in application code, persistence/encryption named by reference to C1 section 6 secrets, not redefined (section 4.2); AC-4 DIRECTORY-POSTURE service account credential scope/storage/rotation/outage fully specified with the function stated explicitly disabled pending corporate verification per D-6 (section 4.4); AC-5 E1-E7 gate chain enumerated in order with each gate's exact check and its composition boundary with C2's own E7/pre-execution checks stated without duplication (section 6);
